lessons.title: Hear what the short forms contain
lessons.description: Get ready for an episode with Misaki, miss a trailer, and ask for a replay.
lessons.canDo: Hear preparation, ongoing actions and obligations in a relaxed conversation.

lessons.title: Recall, wonder and respond among peers
lessons.description: Chat with Kenta the next morning and arrange another viewing.

grammar.title: Hear the full verb inside a short ending
grammar.formation: Vてしまう→Vちゃう; Vでしまう→Vじゃう. Past ちゃった/じゃった.
grammar.explanation: Casual ちゃう/じゃう can describe finishing completely or an unintended outcome. Regret comes from the situation, not every use. Start with the verb’s te-form: 書いて→書いちゃう, 読んで→読んじゃう. These are common peer-speech contractions, not a separate set of verbs.
grammar.example: 早口の返事を聞き逃しちゃった。
grammar.translation: I missed the rapidly spoken reply.

examples.ja: {早口|はやくち}の{返事|へんじ}を{聞|き}き{逃|のが}しちゃった。
examples.en: I missed the rapidly spoken reply.

examples.ja: {短|みじか}い{記事|きじ}を{全部|ぜんぶ}{読|よ}んじゃった。
examples.en: I finished reading the whole short article.

examples.ja: {準備|じゅんび}は{先|さき}にしちゃおう。

grammar.mistake: Do not attach ちゃう to the masu stem: 読みちゃう is not the contraction of 読んでしまう.

grammar.title: Preparation and a current state sound different
grammar.formation: ておく→とく; でおく→どく. ている→てる; でいる→でる. といて/どいて are contracted te-forms.
grammar.explanation: とく keeps the preparation or leave-ready meaning of ておく; てる keeps the ongoing/resulting/habitual meaning of ている. Preserve て/で: 読んでおく→読んどく, 読んでいる→読んでる. Past 読んどいた and 読んでた remain different. Context tells whether でる comes from でいる or is the verb 出る.

examples.ja: {予告|よこく}を{先|さき}に{見|み}とくね。
{今|いま}、{話|はな}し{言葉|ことば}を{聞|き}いてる。
examples.en: I’m listening to spoken language now.

examples.ja: {資料|しりょう}は{先|さき}に{読|よ}んどいて。

grammar.mistake: 見とく is preparing, while 見てる is watching or an ongoing/resulting state. Do not collapse both into one meaning.

grammar.title: Recognise a shortened obligation
grammar.formation: Vない: replace ない with なきゃ or なくちゃ. Often omit following いけない/ならない/だめ. する→しなきゃ; 来る→こなきゃ.
grammar.explanation: A friend can end with 確認しなきゃ to say they need to check. なきゃ comes from なければ and なくちゃ from なくては in necessity expressions. Both are available to different speakers. They express a required action; they are not the prohibition てはいけない.
grammar.example: 始める前に、音量を確認しなきゃ。
grammar.translation: I need to check the volume before starting.

examples.ja: {始|はじ}める{前|まえ}に、{音量|おんりょう}を{確認|かくにん}しなきゃ。
examples.en: I need to check the volume before starting.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{早|はや}く{起|お}きなくちゃ。
examples.en: I have to get up early tomorrow.

examples.ja: {七時|しちじ}までに{来|こ}なきゃ。
examples.en: I have to come by seven.

grammar.mistake: しなきゃ means need to do, not must not do. Use the negative base, not するなきゃ.

grammar.title: Remember a plan; wonder about an answer
grammar.formation: Recall: Vた+っけ; V+んだっけ; N/na-adj+だっけ/だったっけ. Wonder: plain V/i-adj+かな; N/na-adj+かな.
grammar.explanation: っけ asks yourself or a familiar listener to retrieve something you once knew, including a future arrangement. かな wonders about an unresolved thought, though it can also soften an utterance to a listener. The taught nonpast verb recall uses んだっけ. A recalled date is not automatically a past event.
grammar.example: 視聴は何時からだったっけ？
grammar.translation: What time was the viewing from again?

examples.ja: {視聴|しちょう}は{何時|なんじ}からだったっけ？
examples.en: What time was the viewing from again?

examples.ja: {来週|らいしゅう}も{集|あつ}まるんだっけ？
examples.en: Were we getting together next week too?

examples.ja: {語尾|ごび}まで{聞|き}き{取|と}れるかな。
examples.en: I wonder whether I can catch the ending too.

grammar.mistake: Do not treat every っけ question as an event already completed. For the taught noun + かな pattern, don’t insert だ.

grammar.title: A shared point and an explanatory question
grammar.formation: Statement+じゃん. Question: plain V/i-adj+の?; N/na-adj+なの? (rising delivery).
grammar.explanation: じゃん presents a point, reaction or shared confirmation among peers. It doesn’t negate the preceding statement like predicate じゃない. Rising の? asks about an explanation or situation: 見てるの？. Nouns/na-adjectives take な: 好きなの？. The same written の can appear in explanatory statements; context and delivery matter.
grammar.example: もう始まってるじゃん。

examples.ja: もう{始|はじ}まってるじゃん。

examples.en: Are you watching the sequel too?

examples.ja: この{主役|しゅやく}が{好|す}きなの？
examples.en: Do you like this lead character?

grammar.mistake: Do not translate affirmative いいじゃん as not good, or confuse explanatory の? with a possessive noun link.

dialogues.title: A short Saturday viewing session
dialogues.scene: Saturday evening at home. Misaki and Bao get ready for the main feature at seven thirty. Bao misses the trailer while answering a phone call; Misaki rewinds it. They agree on normal speed and a pause every ten minutes.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {本編|ほんぺん}は{七時半|しちじはん}からだったっけ？ {予告|よこく}、{先|さき}に{見|み}とく？
lines.romaji: Honpen wa shichijihan kara datta kke? Yokoku, saki ni mitoku?
lines.meaning: We said seven thirty for the main feature, right? Shall we watch the trailer first?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん。あ、もう{始|はじ}まってるじゃん。{携帯|けいたい}、しまわなきゃ。
lines.romaji: Un. A, mō hajimatteru jan. Keitai, shimawanakya.
lines.meaning: Yeah. Oh, it’s already started! I need to put my phone away.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {今|いま}の{台詞|せりふ}、{早口|はやくち}だったね。{十分|じゅっぷん}ごとに{一時停止|いちじていし}しとく？
lines.romaji: Ima no serifu, hayakuchi datta ne. Juppun goto ni ichiji teishi shitoku?
lines.meaning: That line was fast. Shall we make a point of pausing every ten minutes?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: そうしよう。{聞|き}き{逃|のが}しちゃうから、{止|と}めた{所|ところ}を{巻|ま}き{戻|もど}して、もう{一度|いちど}{再生|さいせい}しなきゃ。
lines.romaji: Sō shiyō. Kikinogashichau kara, tometa tokoro o makimodoshite, mō ichido saisei shinakya.
lines.meaning: Let’s do that. I miss things, so I need to rewind where we stop and play it again.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {今日|きょう}は{倍速|ばいそく}にしないで{見|み}よう。{音量|おんりょう}、{小|ちい}さくしとくね。
lines.romaji: Kyō wa baisoku ni shinai de miyō. Onryō, chiisaku shitoku ne.
lines.meaning: Let’s keep it at normal speed today. I’ll turn the volume down a bit.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: あれ、{主役|しゅやく}は{誰|だれ}だったっけ？ {脇役|わきやく}の{人|ひと}も{出|で}てるじゃん。
lines.romaji: Are, shuyaku wa dare datta kke? Wakiyaku no hito mo deteru jan.
lines.meaning: Wait, who was the lead again? Look, the supporting actor’s in this too.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: え、{予告|よこく}を{見|み}{逃|のが}しちゃったの？ {今|いま}の{所|ところ}、{戻|もど}しとくよ。
lines.romaji: E, yokoku o minogashichatta no? Ima no tokoro, modoshitoku yo.
lines.meaning: Oh, did you miss the trailer? I’ll rewind that bit for you.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん、{電話|でんわ}に{出|で}てたんだ。もう{切|き}ったよ。{字幕|じまく}ばっかり{読|よ}んじゃうから、{今度|こんど}は{声|こえ}も{聞|き}かなきゃ。
lines.romaji: Un, denwa ni deteta n da. Mō kitta yo. Jimaku bakkari yonjau kara, kondo wa koe mo kikanakya.
lines.meaning: Yeah, I was on the phone. I’ve hung up now. I keep just reading the subtitles, so this time I need to listen too.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: いいじゃん。{日本語|にほんご}で{見|み}てるし、{吹|ふ}き{替|か}えにはしなくていいよね。{続編|ぞくへん}は{今日|きょう}も{見|み}るんだっけ？
lines.romaji: Ii jan. Nihongo de miteru shi, fukikae ni wa shinakute ii yo ne. Zokuhen wa kyō mo miru n da kke?

lines.meaning: The sequel can wait. I have to get up early tomorrow. Let’s watch the trailer first, then the main feature.

dialogues.title: Remembering the plan and the actual viewing
dialogues.scene: Sunday morning. Kenta asks about the film he missed. The friends discuss a confusing exchange, avoid spoiling the sequel and realise they still need to pick their next viewing day.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {昨日|きのう}は{何時|なんじ}から{見|み}たんだっけ？ {予告|よこく}だけ？
lines.romaji: Kinō wa nanji kara mita n da kke? Yokoku dake?
lines.meaning: What time did you start watching yesterday again? Just the trailer?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {七時半|しちじはん}から{本編|ほんぺん}も{見|み}たよ。{十分|じゅっぷん}ごとに{止|と}めてたから、{終|お}わるのが{遅|おそ}くなっちゃった。
lines.romaji: Shichijihan kara honpen mo mita yo. Juppun goto ni tometeta kara, owaru no ga osoku nacchatta.
lines.meaning: The main feature too, from seven thirty. We kept pausing every ten minutes, so we finished pretty late.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {二人|ふたり}で「うん」って{言|い}ってる{所|ところ}、どっちが{相|あい}づちで、どっちがつぶやきなのかな。{同|おな}じに{聞|き}こえちゃう。
lines.romaji: Futari de un tte itteru tokoro, docchi ga aizuchi de, docchi ga tsubuyaki na no kana. Onaji ni kikoechau.
lines.meaning: When they both say “mm,” I wonder which is a response and which is muttering. They sound the same to me.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: そこ、{面白|おもしろ}いじゃん。{前|まえ}の{台詞|せりふ}も{聞|き}いてみなきゃ。{僕|ぼく}、{予告|よこく}では{聞|き}き{逃|のが}しちゃったんだ。
lines.romaji: Soko, omoshiroi jan. Mae no serifu mo kiite minakya. Boku, yokoku de wa kikinogashichatta n da.
lines.meaning: That’s interesting! We need to listen to the line before it too. I missed it in the trailer.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: じゃ、そこはメモに{残|のこ}しとくね。{続編|ぞくへん}は{昨日|きのう}も{見|み}てないよ。{結末|けつまつ}、{言|い}っちゃだめだからね。
lines.romaji: Ja, soko wa memo ni nokoshitoku ne. Zokuhen wa kinō mo mitenai yo. Ketsumatsu, itcha dame da kara ne.
lines.meaning: I’ll note that bit for later. We didn’t watch the sequel yesterday either. Don’t spoil the ending!

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: そうだ、{次|つぎ}に{集|あつ}まる{曜日|ようび}って、もう{決|き}めたっけ？ {決|き}めてないなら{連絡|れんらく}しなきゃ。
lines.romaji: Sō da, tsugi ni atsumaru yōbi tte, mō kimeta kke? Kimetenai nara renraku shinakya.
lines.meaning: Oh, did we decide which day to meet next? If we haven’t, we need to get in touch.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: まだじゃない？ {僕|ぼく}も{予定|よてい}を{見|み}とくよ。{昨日|きのう}の{音量|おんりょう}はどうだった？
lines.romaji: Mada ja nai? Boku mo yotei o mitoku yo. Kinō no onryō wa dō datta?
lines.meaning: I don’t think so. I’ll check my schedule too. How was the volume yesterday?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {小|ちい}さくしたけど、{台詞|せりふ}は{聞|き}こえてたよ。{倍速|ばいそく}にはしてない。バオが{合図|あいず}したら、{元|もと}の{場面|ばめん}に{戻|もど}してた。
lines.romaji: Chiisaku shita kedo, serifu wa kikoeteta yo. Baisoku ni wa shitenai. Bao ga aizu shitara, moto no bamen ni modoshiteta.
lines.meaning: It was low, but we could hear the lines. We didn’t use double speed. Whenever Bao signalled, I went back to the scene.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {途中|とちゅう}で{眠気|ねむけ}が{出|で}ちゃったけどね。{毎回|まいかい}、{短|みじか}い{休息|きゅうそく}も{入|い}れとくといいかも。
lines.romaji: Tochū de nemuke ga dechatta kedo ne. Maikai, mijikai kyūsoku mo iretoku to ii kamo.
lines.meaning: I did get sleepy halfway through, though. Maybe we should plan a short break each time too.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: いいじゃん。{次|つぎ}は{僕|ぼく}も{見|み}たいな。{曜日|ようび}が{決|き}まったら{教|おし}えて。{忘|わす}れないようにメモしとく。
lines.romaji: Ii jan. Tsugi wa boku mo mitai na. Yōbi ga kimattara oshiete. Wasurenai yō ni memo shitoku.
lines.meaning: Sounds good. I’d like to watch next time too. Tell me when you pick a day. I’ll write it down so I don’t forget.

バオは{着信|ちゃくしん}に{応答|おうとう}していて、{最初|さいしょ}の{予告|よこく}を{見|み}{逃|のが}しちゃった。{携帯|けいたい}をしまってから、もう{一度|いちど}{見|み}たよ。{小|ちい}さな{音量|おんりょう}でも{台詞|せりふ}は{聞|き}こえた。{分|わ}からない{語尾|ごび}はメモに{残|のこ}して、{毎回|まいかい}{確認|かくにん}することにした。
{次|つぎ}の{予定|よてい}は、まだ{決|き}まってない。{曜日|ようび}を{決|き}めたら{連絡|れんらく}するね。{疲労|ひろう}や{眠気|ねむけ}が{出|で}たら、{休息|きゅうそく}を{入|い}れなくちゃ。{短|みじか}い{練習|れんしゅう}なら{続|つづ}けられるかな。ミサキ

glosses.meaning: have not watched; 見ていない
missed seeing; 見逃してしまった
put away; not a てしまう contraction here
not yet settled; 決まっていない

exercises.prompt: When will they start the main feature?
exercises.explain: Misaki recalls 七時半 for the main feature and Bao agrees; the scene takes place on Saturday evening.

exercises.prompt: How will they handle fast speech?
options: Pause every ten minutes and replay the stopped part
Keep watching the sequel without pausing
exercises.explain: They agree on 十分ごとに一時停止 and on rewinding and replaying the part where they stop.

exercises.prompt: Why has Bao not seen the first preview?
options: He was answering an incoming call
He was copying the minutes in the room
He had already seen the sequel
exercises.explain: Bao says 電話に出てたんだ: he was on the phone when the trailer played.

exercises.context: Form practice: you finished reading the sequel to a book. Shorten 読んでしまった to its named casual contraction.
exercises.line: {続編|ぞくへん}を{全部|ぜんぶ}{読|よ}ん＿＿。
exercises.explain: 読んで ends with で: でしまった→じゃった.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the named preparatory contraction of 見ておく, not the ongoing form.
exercises.line: {先|さき}に{予告|よこく}を{見|み}＿＿ね。
exercises.explain: 見ておく→見とく. 見てる describes watching/a state; 見ちゃった is past completion.

exercises.context: Your friend says they missed the preview while answering a call. Suggest replaying it before the main feature.
exercises.line: {電話|でんわ}に{出|で}てて、{予告|よこく}を{見|み}{逃|のが}しちゃった。
options: じゃ、{本編|ほんぺん}の{前|まえ}にもう{一度|いちど}{見|み}よう。
じゃ、{予告|よこく}はもう{全部|ぜんぶ}{見|み}たんだね。
じゃ、{続編|ぞくへん}まで{終|お}わったんだね。
exercises.explain: The first offers a replay. The others falsely treat unseen material as already watched.

exercises.meaning: Before viewing, I need to decide the rest times. Use 決めなきゃ.
exercises.explain: 決めない→決めなきゃ. This is the speaker’s obligation, not a prohibition.

exercises.prompt: What does Misaki say they did NOT watch on Saturday?
exercises.explain: She explicitly says 昨日は続編を見てない; they watched both preview and main feature.

exercises.prompt: What is Bao wondering whether he can distinguish?
options: Permission and compulsion at the workplace
The day and time already set for next week
exercises.explain: Bao says 相づちとつぶやきも区別できるかな; it’s his unresolved learning question.

options: At a lowered but audible volume, without double speed
exercises.explain: Misaki says 台詞は聞こえた and 倍速にせず.

exercises.context: Form practice: ask a familiar friend to recall the agreed time, using the named だったっけ pattern.
exercises.line: {視聴|しちょう}は{七時半|しちじはん}から＿＿？
exercises.explain: For noun/time recall, だった+っけ. This can recall an arrangement, not only a past action.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the explanatory casual の question after the na-adjective 好き.
exercises.line: この{主役|しゅやく}が{好|す}き＿＿？
exercises.explain: 好き is na-adjectival: 好きなの？. Verbs/i-adjectives attach の directly.

exercises.context: Your friend feels sleepy. Propose taking a short rest before the next scene, without dismissing the tiredness.
options: じゃ、{次|つぎ}の{場面|ばめん}の{前|まえ}に{短|みじか}い{休息|きゅうそく}を{入|い}れよう。
じゃ、{眠気|ねむけ}は{全|まった}くないんだね。
じゃ、{音量|おんりょう}はもう{決|き}まったんだね。
exercises.explain: The first answers the reported sleepiness with a rest. The other replies deny it or change the topic.

exercises.line: {小|ちい}さくしたけど、{台詞|せりふ}は{聞|き}こえてたよ。{倍速|ばいそく}にはしてない。バオが{合図|あいず}したら、{元|もと}の{場面|ばめん}に{戻|もど}してた。
exercises.prompt: Who reports that the lines were audible and the scene was replayed on a signal?
exercises.explain: Misaki answers Kenta’s volume question and describes replaying when Bao signals.

exercises.meaning: I’ll note the ending beforehand and check it each time. Use the contracted preparatory 残しといて.
tiles: メモに{残|のこ}しといて、
exercises.explain: 残しておいて→残しといて prepares a note for later checking.

exercises.prompt: What date/time does the message report as the actual main-feature viewing?
exercises.explain: The message is sent Sunday morning, but explicitly reports Saturday seven thirty.

exercises.prompt: What is the status of their next viewing day?
options: It has not been decided; Misaki will contact Kenta after deciding
It’s a workplace assignment on Wednesday
exercises.explain: 次の予定は、まだ決まってない and 曜日を決めたら連絡する distinguish unset plans from remembered Saturday.

exercises.prompt: What did Bao do after putting away the phone?
options: Watched the sequel at double speed
exercises.explain: 携帯をしまってから、もう一度見た refers back to the missed preview.

grammar: とく/どく vs てる/でる
じゃん and explanatory の?
watch.prompt: Optionally save a contracted line from your own clip. Write its full form and identify the speaker and listener. Listen for the ending before checking subtitles.

recycling.reason: Film-night peers use repeated casual contractions. Equipment reports, minutes and private-work documents do not belong in their conversation.
